definitions.explanation: The whitish, chalky film left behind when tap water evaporates, made up of minerals in the water. Builds up on sinks, bathroom mirrors, kettles, and faucets.

examples.japanese: ⟦{鏡|かがみ}→鏡：02190_kagami⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{水垢|みずあか}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧ついて⟦いる→いる：00495_iru⟧。
examples.english: There are water stains on the mirror.

examples.english: Limescale comes off well if you use citric acid.

examples.english: Limescale had built up around the faucet, so I scrubbed it off with a toothbrush.

notes:
A staple word in cleaning advice and household-product labels.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {水垢|みずあか}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧つく: limescale forms
- {水垢|みずあか}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{落|お}とす→落とす：01246_otosu⟧: to remove limescale
- {水垢|みずあか}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧たまる: limescale builds up
- {水垢|みずあか}{取|と}り: a limescale remover

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦カビ→カビ：07055_kabi⟧: mold — black or green growth, a living organism rather than a mineral deposit
- ⟦{湯垢|ゆあか}→湯垢：30416_yuaka⟧: scale from hot water, kettle scale — the same deposit seen inside kettles and bathtubs
- よごれ: dirt, grime — the general word covering any kind of soiling
